h: From Earls to Hare Krishna and Back Again
p: Croome Court was the home of the Earls of Coventry, and it was the 6th Earl who brought in the big names in the eighteenth century. Croome was Capability Brown's first major commission for a complete landscape, and Robert Adam designed some of the interiors. Over the twentieth century, the house had some remarkable lives: it was a boarding school, then for a time in the late 1970s and early 1980s it was owned by the Hare Krishna movement, and later it passed through several private owners before the National Trust took it on. Each chapter has left its mark.

Near the visitor centre, the old wartime buildings tell the story of RAF Defford, where top-secret work on radar was tested in the skies over Worcestershire. Many of the people involved were sworn to secrecy for decades, so it's fascinating to hear their stories now.

Look out for the church of St Mary Magdalene on its rise above the park, part of Brown's grand plan, and the various temples and follies placed to catch your eye across the landscape. On a clear day the Malvern Hills make a superb backdrop.

Allow half a day or more. Worcester is close enough for an afternoon add-on, while Great Malvern, with its spring water and hilltop walks, is a short drive away for anyone who wants to stretch their legs further.
